adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and each is looked up via `User.find_by_username(username)`; if the user is not found it is skipped, and the method still proceeds to `group.save` and returns `success_json` on save (no indication of skipped usernames). This makes it impossible to distinguish successful adds from typos. However, the same “silent success on non-existent users” behavior existed previously in `update_patch` (now removed) and even had a spec covering it, suggesting this is a product/UX/API design issue rather than a newly introduced correctness defect.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new membership-related AJAX flows do not attach any explicit rejection handling: `findMembers`, `removeMember`, and `addMembers` in `group.js` only use `.then(...)` (or just return the `Discourse.ajax(...)` promise) with no `.catch`/failure callback, and controller actions like `next`/`previous`/`removeMember`/`addMembers` likewise don’t handle rejections (e.g., `bootbox.confirm` callback calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` without handling errors). However, the claim that errors are “swallowed with no feedback” can’t be proven from the diff alone because global AJAX/promise error handling may exist elsewhere; what is verifiable is the absence of local error-handling/UX around failures, and that refreshes only happen on the success path (`.then(...)`).

The UI-side part is verifiable: `addMembers` in `admin-group.js.es6` has a TODO and does not clear/reset `this.get("usernames")` after adding, so the same usernames remain in the input and a second click will re-submit them.

adjudication.rationale: In the public groups members flow, `GroupsController#members` now always paginates with a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `offset` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb), and the client `Discourse.Group#findMembers` always requests `/groups/<name>/members.json` with `limit`/`offset` defaults of 50/0 (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js). The `group-members` route now sets `controller.model` to the group and calls `model.findMembers()` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6), while the template only switches iteration to `{{#each m in members}}` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) and does not add any pagination controls to change `offset` or load subsequent pages. Therefore, groups with >50 members will only ever show the first 50 in the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin update happy path has no coverage after the param-format change: the only surviving update test is the automatic-group name-ignore case, and nothing tests the new flat params (params[:name], params[:alias_level], params[:visible] — the nested params[:group][...] format was dropped) or that a non-automatic group can actually be renamed or have alias_level changed; a parsing regression would pass the entire suite while breaking group rename/alias_level/visible for every admin

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#update to consume flat params (params[:alias_level], params[:visible], params[:name]) instead of the previous nested payload (params[:group][...]) and removes the old update specs that exercised renaming/updating fields. In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb the only remaining update coverage is the automatic-group name-ignore test; there is no test that a non-automatic group can be renamed, that alias_level persists, or that visible toggles via the new param shape. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap that could allow a params/parsing regression to slip through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The remove_member 422 test issues the wrong HTTP verb: it uses xhr :put, :remove_member while the route is delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'; controller specs bypass routing, so the test passes regardless of verb, cannot catch a route/method mismatch (e.g., moving the bare member routes into a collection block would drop params[:group_id] and 400 in production while the suite stays green), and misdocuments the API
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out the same underlying issue: the remove_member test uses xhr :put while the route for groups#remove_member is defined with the DELETE verb, meaning the test is using the wrong HTTP method relative to routing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Edge-case coverage was deleted with the old PATCH tests and not re-created for the new endpoints: the new add_members/remove_member actions preserve the silent-success behaviors (succeeding silently when adding non-existent users and when removing non-members) but nothing tests them now, so a regression would silently drop members while still returning a success response

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior PATCH “incremental” specs that explicitly asserted silent-success behavior for edge cases (adding a non-existent user and removing a non-member) in `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` (the whole `context 'incremental'` block is deleted). The new endpoint specs added under `context ".add_members"` and `context ".remove_member"` only cover adding valid users and removing an existing member, plus automatic-group rejection, but do not reintroduce assertions for those edge cases. The controller implementations still appear to preserve the silent behavior (`add_members` skips when `User.find_by_username` returns nil; `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` which is typically a no-op if not a member), so the issue is specifically missing regression coverage for the new endpoints, not a demonstrated runtime defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding a username that is already a member is untested — the naive group.add(user) path may raise on a duplicate GroupUser record and return a 500

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code loops usernames and calls `group.add(user)` without checking whether the user is already in the group (`usernames.split(",").each ... group.add(user)`). The new controller spec for `.add_members` only tests adding two distinct users and does not cover adding an existing member, so this edge-case is untested. Whether it actually raises/500s depends on how `Group#add`/the join model handles duplicates (not shown in the diff), so the asserted 500 is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Usernames with surrounding spaces are silently skipped after the bare split(',') in add_members — untested

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace. If the client submits `"alice, bob"` (note the space), `" bob"` will not match a username and will be silently skipped. The added specs for `.add_members` only cover comma-joined usernames without spaces, so this edge case is not tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The params.require 400 paths for the new add/remove member endpoints are untested

adjudication.rationale: The new Admin::GroupsController endpoints `add_members` and `remove_member` use `params.require(:group_id)` and `params.require(:usernames)` / `params.require(:user_id)` (which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` and typically produce a 400). The added specs under `context ".add_members"` and `context ".remove_member"` only cover the success path and the automatic-group 422 path, and always pass the required params; there is no test exercising missing-param/400 behavior for these new endpoints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: render_json_error branches are untested across the admin controller: no test exercises invalid input (blank name, name containing spaces, duplicate name) reaching render_json_error in create, update, or add_members, leaving the 422 error contract surfaced by the admin frontend completely unpinned

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds/changes several controller actions that call `render_json_error` on save failure: `Admin::GroupsController#create` (lines where `if group.save ... else render_json_error group`), `#update` (same pattern), and `#add_members`/`#remove_member` (same pattern). The updated spec (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`) exercises happy paths (successful create/update/destroy/add/remove) and automatic-group rejection (422), but does not include any cases that force `group.save` to fail and thus execute the `render_json_error` branches. The specific invalid inputs mentioned (blank name, spaces-only name after strip, duplicate name) are plausible failure modes but validations are not shown in the diff, so the core verifiable issue is the untested error branches/422 contract for these new/modified endpoints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No JS test work accompanies ~150 lines of new frontend behavior: findMembers/removeMember/addMembers in group.js and the new admin-group.js.es6 actions are all untested, leaving the add → reload → user_count/members update flow with no safety net

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new client-side logic without adding any corresponding JS/frontend tests. New/changed behavior includes: `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now performs a paginated AJAX request and mutates `user_count/limit/offset/members` (group.js), new `removeMember` and `addMembers` methods that trigger reloads, and new controller actions `next/previous/removeMember/addMembers` plus pagination computed properties (admin-group.js.es6). The only tests added/modified in this diff are Ruby controller specs (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb); there are no QUnit/Ember/frontend tests covering the add → reload → members/user_count update flow mentioned in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers now returns undefined instead of a promise when the group name is empty — an unpinned contract change where any future caller chaining .then() breaks silently

Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no way to page: findMembers() was rewritten around the admin page's needs with limit/offset/user_count baked into the shared model and every call capped at 50, while the public group.members route calls model.findMembers() as-is and its template iterates members with no pagination controls and never advances offset

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination with a default `limit` of 50 (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`), and rewrites `Discourse.Group#findMembers()` to call `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit`/`offset` taken from the shared Group model defaults (`limit: 50`, `offset: 0`). The public `group-members` route now does `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();` and the public template iterates `{{#each m in members}}` without any pagination controls or any logic to advance `offset`. From the diff alone, public group members pages will only ever fetch/render the first 50 members, with no UI path shown here to request subsequent pages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages off-by-one creates a phantom empty last page: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit); when user_count % limit == 0, totalPages is one too high, so 'next' stays enabled on the real last page and clicking it requests offset == user_count, returning zero rows and looking like data loss

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is off-by-one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100/50 -> 3 instead of 2). Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to this inflated `totalPages`, the "next" action remains enabled on the real last page. Clicking next sets `offset` to `Math.min(offset+limit, user_count)` (so it can become exactly `user_count`), and `Group.findMembers` then requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with `offset == user_count`, which `GroupsController#members` will return as an empty `members` list. This matches the reported phantom empty last page behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Offset-clamping invariant is implemented twice: both the admin controller (next/previous actions) and findMembers in the model independently enforce that offset must lie in [0, user_count], so the same paging rule has two owners that must be found and updated together whenever the rule changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows offset bounds enforced in two places: (1) admin-group controller actions clamp before setting the model offset (next: `Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`, previous: `Math.max(..., 0)`), and (2) `Discourse.Group#findMembers` independently clamps the offset before issuing the request (`offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`). This is a real “two owners for the same paging invariant” maintainability concern, not a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers return contract is now inconsistent: the empty-name path returns undefined while every other path returns an RSVP.Promise (the old code returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([])), so any future .then() caller throws on the undefined path
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that some code paths in the function do not explicitly return a value, causing `undefined` to be returned (specifically the empty-name path), leading to inconsistent return behavior compared to other paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create silently discards the alias_level the client sends: the client's asJSON() includes alias_level and the admin 'new group' form renders the alias-level combo box, but the server's create only reads name and visible, so the group always gets alias_level 0 and must be edited again

adjudication.rationale: Client-side `Discourse.Group.asJSON()` includes `alias_level` and the admin group form always renders the alias-level combo-box (`group.hbs`), and `create()` POSTs `data: this.asJSON()`. But `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` and never reads/sets `params[:alias_level]`, so the selected alias level is ignored on creation and the group will use the model default (likely 0) until edited later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group-name normalization is enforced on create but not on update: creating strips params[:name] but the update path assigns group.name = params[:name] without stripping, so renaming an existing group to ' bob ' stores the whitespace-padded name, violating the no-spaces rule and breaking group-mention handling

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#create the name is normalized via `(params[:name] || '').strip`, but in Admin::GroupsController#update the rename path assigns `group.name = params[:name]` (when not automatic) without stripping. The diff shows no equivalent normalization on update, so an existing group can be renamed to a whitespace-padded value (e.g. " bob "), diverging from create behavior and the UI expectation of no spaces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers ships acknowledged-incomplete behavior: after a successful add the usernames field is not cleared (marked with a TODO), so the just-added names remain in the input and clicking 'Add' again re-submits them

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `addMembers` action contains an explicit `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not reset `this.usernames` after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))`. From the diff, nothing else clears the bound `user-selector` value, so the entered usernames can remain in the input and could be resubmitted by clicking “Add” again. This is a concrete, diff-grounded UX/incompleteness issue, but not a clearly verifiable correctness defect (duplicate-handling/server behavior isn’t shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec exercises remove_member with the wrong HTTP verb: the 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec uses xhr :put while the route and the sibling 'is able to remove a member' spec use DELETE; controller specs bypass routing, so the suite no longer pins the verb/routing contract for this action

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` under context `.remove_member`, the test `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, while `config/routes.rb` wires `remove_member` to `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`) and the adjacent spec `"is able to remove a member"` correctly uses `xhr :delete`. Because controller specs invoke actions directly, this `:put` call won’t fail due to routing/verb mismatch and thus no longer enforces the intended DELETE contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking shape change to the public /groups/:name/members.json response: the endpoint went from a bare serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no versioning or compatibility shim, silently breaking plugins/external clients that may consume this guardian-guarded API

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` (object with `members` + `meta`) while keeping the same route (`/groups/:group_id/members`, now requested as `/members.json` in JS). This is an intentional API shape change that can break any external/plugin client that previously consumed the array response, but it’s not an internal correctness defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No bounds on the public limit/offset params: limit is whatever the client sends (one request can pull an entire membership list in a single query) and offset is unvalidated, with negative values flowing straight into Relation#offset

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, pagination params are taken directly from the client: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then applied as `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no upper bound on `limit`, so a client can request an arbitrarily large membership list in one query, and `offset` can be negative (e.g. "-10".to_i => -10) and is passed straight into `Relation#offset`, which can yield invalid SQL/DB errors or unintended behavior. This behavior is introduced by the diff (previous logic limited automatic groups and defaulted offset safely).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Routes fire findMembers() and discard the promise: both the admin group route and the public group-members route previously returned the members promise from afterModel, but now setupController calls model.findMembers() fire-and-forget, so a failed request leaves a silently empty member list with no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes both routes from returning the members-loading promise in `afterModel` to calling `model.findMembers()` inside `setupController` without returning/awaiting it (`admin_group_route.js` and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`). Since `findMembers()` returns an AJAX promise (or `undefined` when name is empty), any rejection will no longer be part of the route's model hook promise chain, so Ember route error substates/handlers tied to the transition won’t run. On failure, `members` never gets set in `Discourse.Group.findMembers()` (it only sets `members` inside `.then(...)`), so the UI can remain empty with no route-level error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls — a regression: the public route calls model.findMembers() with no arguments (using the default limit: 50) and no pagination was wired, whereas previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups defaulted to 200, so members silently disappear from the page on active sites

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `offset`, returning only a page of members (`limit(limit).offset(offset)`) for *all* groups (not just automatic). The public `group-members` route still calls `model.findMembers()` with no pagination UI/controls added in `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`, so only the first 50 members are loaded and displayed (`{{#each m in members}}`). Previously, non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups defaulted to 200, so this introduces silent truncation on the public members page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields a phantom empty page whenever user_count % limit == 0 (should be Math.ceil), and the offset clamp Math.min(offset + limit, user_count) wrongly permits offset == user_count, so clicking 'next' on the real last page loads a blank page

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count % limit == 0` (e.g., 100/50 => 3 pages instead of 2). The `next` action also clamps `offset` with `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, allowing `offset == user_count`; `group.findMembers()` then requests that offset (it clamps to `<= user_count`), which would return an empty `members` page. This matches the finding: a phantom blank last page is reachable by clicking next from the real last page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames is never cleared in the admin group controller — stale input leaks across groups: usernames is now a plain property on a singleton controller and setupController only resets model, so unsubmitted text typed on group A is submitted to group B, and the input is not cleared after a successful add so clicking Add re-submits the same usernames

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `usernames` was changed from a computed property tied to `members` to a plain controller field (`usernames: null`). In `admin_group_route.js`, `setupController` now only sets `model` and calls `model.findMembers()`; it does not reset `controller.usernames`. Since Ember route controllers are singletons, any text entered into `{{user-selector usernames=usernames}}` can persist when switching between groups. Additionally, `actions.addMembers` contains a `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not clear `this.get("usernames")` after calling `model.addMembers(...)`, so clicking Add again will resubmit the same usernames unless the user manually edits the field.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips unknown usernames (and untrimmed entries like ' alice' after a comma-space split) and returns success_json even when zero users were added — the UI reloads the member list and no error is surfaced anywhere

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, `usernames.split(",")` does not trim entries, so inputs like "alice, bob" will attempt `User.find_by_username(" bob")` and silently skip the user. Unknown usernames are also silently skipped (`if user = ...`), and the action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero users were added. On the client, Group#addMembers always reloads members on success and does not surface any error state, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members and remove_member are not transactional: HABTM group.add(user) and group.users.delete(user_id) persist join rows immediately, so if a later iteration raises or the trailing group.save fails with 422, earlier adds/removals are already committed while the client is told the request failed, leaving the UI showing a stale list

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members and #remove_member (new in this diff), the code mutates the HABTM association via `group.add(user)` inside a loop and `group.users.delete(user_id)` before checking `if group.save ... else render_json_error`. In Rails HABTM/has_many-through association updates generally write the join rows immediately; the trailing `group.save` does not wrap those changes. If an exception occurs mid-loop or if `group.save` returns false (rendering 422), earlier join-row adds/removals may already be committed while the client is told the request failed, matching the reported inconsistency/stale UI risk. The diff shows no transaction around these operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create silently discards alias_level: the client's asJSON() sends it and the admin UI shows the alias-level combo, but create only persists name and visible, so a group created with an alias level selected silently gets alias_level: 0 (pre-existing, but both sides were rewritten here without fixing it)

adjudication.rationale: In the client, `Discourse.Group.asJSON()` includes `alias_level` and `create()` POSTs it (`data: this.asJSON()`), and the admin template still binds the alias level combo to `alias_level`. But `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` (no `alias_level`), so any selected alias level is ignored on creation and will default (likely 0). This is a real behavior defect exposed by the rewrite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking API change without versioning: GET /groups/:name/members changed from a flat JSON array to {members: [...], meta: {...}}, breaking external consumers/plugins

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to return an object `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` (see `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`) instead of the previous `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`, which would have returned a flat serialized collection. The frontend was updated accordingly (JS now calls `/members.json` and reads `result.members`/`result.meta`). This is a real, diff-grounded API response-shape change that could break external consumers/plugins relying on the old array format, but it’s not an internal correctness defect shown by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Old-style membership API calls silently no-op: PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes: {add/delete} and PUT with group: {usernames} fall through to the new update action, which ignores those keys entirely and returns success_json — a 200 no-op instead of a 410/422

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the old request shapes are no longer handled: it now reads only top-level `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]` (and ignores rename for automatic groups). The previous logic that handled `request.patch?` with `params[:changes][:add/delete]` and `params[:group][:usernames]` was removed. Therefore, legacy clients sending `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: {add/delete}` or `PUT` with `group: {usernames: ...}` will fall into the new `update`, apply no membership changes (and likely no other changes, since `params[:name]` etc. are nested), yet still `group.save` and return `success_json` (200) — a silent no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded and negative limit/offset on the public members endpoint: ?limit=99999999 triggers a count plus full load and serialization of every user in a large group (cheap amplification query on a publicly reachable route), and negative values like ?limit=-1 or ?offset=-1 pass into limit()/offset() and produce DB errors/500s

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff now reads `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then unconditionally executes `total = group.users.count` and `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serializes `members` (JSON response with `serialize_data`). There is no validation/clamping of `limit`/`offset` to a sane max or to non-negative values. This makes `?limit=99999999` request an arbitrarily large page (potentially loading/serializing most/all group users) and `?limit=-1`/`?offset=-1` pass negative values into ActiveRecord `limit/offset`, which can cause errors/500s depending on adapter/version. The endpoint is a public (non-admin) controller action guarded only by `guardian.ensure_can_see!`, so it is reachable by regular users for visible groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New <form> wrapper in the admin group template: pressing Enter in the group-name field or user-selector input triggers native implicit form submission to the current URL — a full page reload that discards unsaved edits, since only the save/delete buttons' {{action}} handlers preventDefault

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps the admin group editor in a plain `<form class="form-horizontal">` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs) but does not attach any Ember `{{action}}` handler to the form’s submit event. Inside the form, the Save/Delete controls are `<button {{action "save"}} ...>` / `<button {{action "destroy"}} ...>` without an explicit `type`, so they default to `type="submit"` in HTML. Pressing Enter in the `text-field` (group name) or the user-selector input can trigger the form’s native implicit submission, which would perform a real browser navigation/reload unless prevented; nothing in the template prevents the submit event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Out-of-order findMembers responses can clobber pagination state: next, previous, addMembers, and removeMember all trigger findMembers() and each response unconditionally setProperties({user_count, limit, offset, members}) with no sequencing/abortion, so if concurrent requests resolve out of order the model ends up with a stale page's offset/members/user_count and the page indicator disagrees with the list

adjudication.rationale: In Discourse.Group#findMembers the AJAX promise always `.then` calls `self.setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members: ... })` based on the response (group.js). Multiple UI actions (`next`/`previous` in admin-group.js.es6, and `addMembers`/`removeMember` which call `findMembers()` again after their own requests) can trigger overlapping `findMembers()` calls without any abort/sequencing/token check. If requests resolve out of order, an older response can overwrite `offset`/`members`/`user_count` with stale values, making pagination state and displayed members inconsistent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members template {{#each m in members}} depends on controller proxying to the model that isn't included in this diff — if GroupMembersController is auto-generated as a plain Ember.Controller, the page renders an empty list; a proxying controller or members property must exist

adjudication.rationale: In `group/members.hbs` the loop was changed from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`, but `group-members` route `setupController` only does `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();`. `findMembers()` now sets `members` on the *Group model* (`self.setProperties({ members: ... })`), not on the controller. Unless the `GroupMembersController` is an `Ember.ObjectController` (or otherwise proxies/aliases `members` to `model.members`), `members` will be undefined in the template and the list will render empty. The diff itself does not add such a proxy/alias.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec calls the DELETE remove_member endpoint with xhr :put (wrong verb for a route wired as delete 'members'), and controller specs invoke actions directly bypassing route recognition, so nothing in the suite exercises the actual DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members wiring or the :group_id param name — the suite stays green even if the route/param plumbing breaks

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires `remove_member` to a DELETE route (`config/routes.rb`: `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`), but the spec’s first `remove_member` example calls it with `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb). Because controller specs invoke the action directly (not via route recognition) and the controller action doesn’t enforce HTTP verb, the test can pass even if the DELETE route/plumbing is broken. This is a test/coverage issue rather than a production behavior defect introduced by the diff.
